provenance.signature: overlay (PolyTree64/PolyTreeD nesting): a result ring whose every vertex lies on the boundary of the ring containing it is put one level too high: an inscribed hole becomes a second top-level node (a direct child of the root, IsHole false, clockwise), an inscribed island becomes a second hole (IsHole true, counter-clockwise); the flat Paths64 result is right. Path2ContainsPath1 (clipper.h:739) returns false when no vertex is strictly inside, so RecursiveCheckOwners (clipper.engine.cpp:2958-2981) drops the correct owner; also when one vertex is rounded just outside. Regression from e8ebdef (#957 fix), since 1.5.3; the symptom #973 reported, whose fix (0d0ba0f) did not cover this case

main + patch/prototype_fix.diff: correct; Clipper2 CPP/Tests 48/48 (and USINGZ build 48/48); 1804-case set: only the 5 lead cases change; random inscribed configurations 4434/4574 wrong -> 0/1 (the 1 is a flat-result near-miss)
provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage; not yet reported (FINAL.md is the drafted report). A remaining case of the regression #973 reported: #973 had the same symptom (a hole at the top level) from the same commit e8ebdef, and its fix (0d0ba0f/927daf7) repaired that input but kept the return false, so FINAL.md is framed as a follow-up to #973. Not a duplicate: no open or closed issue or PR has this input (20 open issues, #1058-#1112, checked 2026-09-26). #942 is an earlier nesting bug with a different mechanism; open #1084 (C#, no data) is loosely related at most; #1008 / Discussion #1022 is valid but non-canonical output, where Angus declined tweaks to results that correctly describe the filled regions, so FINAL.md stresses that the PolyTree ownership contract, not the region, is broken; open PR #1101 still reproduces. Severity: wrong structure, not wrong region. The rings, the flat Paths64 result and the tree's signed-area sum are exact; only PolyTree parent links are wrong, so the error is gross only for code that reads the tree (OGC-read area 20 vs 12 on the minimal case, 4166 vs 2010 on a lead case) and shows up as overlay results that are wrong when read as OGC polygons (adapter), not in v1 areas. Clipper2's own tests miss it: CheckPolytreeFullyContainsChildren only checks nodes that have children, and TestPolytreeHoles2 compares signed areas. The 93 % fuzz figure holds within a deliberately degenerate family (every vertex of B on A's boundary). Lead case hole-contact-7-000044 is the rounding variant (one island vertex snapped just outside its hole) of the same return false. C# port keeps the old midpoint fallback (probably unaffected); Delphi has the same Exit (probably affected); neither was run. The PolyTree64 doc sentences came through web search and the #957 text only (angusj.com and web.archive.org blocked in the sandbox): FINAL.md cites only clipper.engine.h and IsHole(); check the docs in a browser before citing them. The 3 other adapter nesting/orientation mismatches on the 1804-case set (int-grid-7-000041, tiny-rotation-1-000108/179) and the fuzz near-miss (A=(-51,59)(-41,24)(-26,-21), B=(-49,52)(-37,12)(-41,27): Difference 16.5, exact 27.5) are flat-result integer-grid effects, not this finding, untriaged.

provenance.notes: By design: the grid is i_overlay's precision model, which i_overlay documents and the geo maintainers know about (commit 4915dfc, discussion #1215), but geo's BooleanOps API documentation does not mention it. ISSUE.md holds a draft documentation/enhancement request for georust/geo (not posted), not a bug report. georust/geo#1493 (closed) shows the same mechanism in a mild form. The rust-geo adapter manifest's delta (grid) covers this behaviour. The repro crate is built and run by run.sh.

provenance.signature: relate and predicates (RelateNG): a ring vertex in the interior of another ring's edge of the same polygonal operand (MultiPolygon parts touching vertex-to-edge, or a hole touching its shell at a hole vertex), with a boundary edge of the other operand along that ring edge, gives a wrong matrix: a MultiPolygon neither contains nor covers its own first part (2F2F11212, exact 2F2F11FF2) and overlaps is true
verified_on: GEOS main ae9cdd98be4e0bae552b918d4d14c94a9ce99c58: wrong
GEOS 3.14.1 (Shapely 2.2.0rc1 wheel) and 3.13.1 (Shapely 2.1.2 wheel): wrong
GEOS 3.11.4 (Shapely 2.0.7 wheel, before RelateNG): correct
JTS master 3ea61f8 and 1.20.0 with RelateNG: wrong; JTS's default RelateOp: correct
provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage; not yet reported. FINAL.md is the report drafted for libgeos/geos and JTS_FINAL.md the one for locationtech/jts (same code, same matrices). Cause: RelateGeometry::isSelfNodingRequired() is false for polygonal operands, so the touch point gets no node section for the ring whose edge passes through it. No duplicate was found; the linked GEOS issues were checked and are different problems. Both operands are valid: OGC allows MultiPolygon parts, and a hole and its shell, to touch at points.

provenance.signature: relate and predicates (RelateNG), polygon/polygon: when the computed point of a proper segment crossing rounds exactly onto a vertex of one operand, RelateNG treats the crossing as a touch at that vertex and loses it: touches = true instead of overlaps (FF2F01212, exact 212101212), or contains/covers (within/covered_by) = true instead of overlaps (212F01FF2)
verified_on: GEOS main ae9cdd98be4e0bae552b918d4d14c94a9ce99c58: wrong
GEOS 3.15.0 and 3.14.1 (built from source), 3.13.1 (Shapely 2.1.2 wheel): wrong
GEOS 3.11.4 (Shapely 2.0.7 wheel, before RelateNG): correct
JTS master 3ea61f8 and 1.20.0, RelateNG.relate: wrong; Geometry.relate (RelateOp): correct
provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage; not yet reported. FINAL.md is the report drafted for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md the one for locationtech/jts. RelateNG's package documentation says numerical round-off may give incorrect answers (first link); FINAL.md explains why this case is still treated as within the contract: the inputs are valid and used as given, LineIntersector's exact orientation tests report the proper crossing that RelateNG then discards, RelateOp gets it right, and the answer contradicts GEOS's own point predicates and depends on the ring's start vertex. The other links are related reports, not duplicates (RelateNGRobustnessTest asserts 2F2101212 for PostGIS 5362 and GIS.SE 484691, a matrix two valid polygons cannot have); no existing report of this behaviour was found.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. FINAL.md is the report drafted for libgeos/geos; it inlines prototype_fix.diff verbatim (applies to ae9cdd98). All three defects are in StructuredCollection (src/geom/HeuristicOverlay.cpp): doSymDifference computes one-sided DIFFERENCE for lines and points (lines 505-528); doDifference subtracts A's own lines instead of a.getLineUnion() from A's points (lines 488-491); the dimension of an operand without non-empty elements stays Dimension::DONTCARE (HeuristicOverlay.h:67), so OverlayUtil::createEmptyResult(-3) asserts. Contract: cases 1a, 1b, 1e, 3a-3c meet even OverlayNG's own input requirements (simple GCs) and GEOS*Prec_r(..., 0) gets them right; the mixed-GC cases are supported by the public API since 3.12 (NEWS 3.12.0 'Support mixed GeometryCollection in overlay ops (GH-797)', implemented by PR #923 'Overlay with mixed dimension'), and the C API documents no restriction (the C++ Geometry.h '@throws IllegalArgumentException for a non-empty GeometryCollection' is stale). D1 on mixed GCs, D2, D4 and D5 date from #923 (3.12.0); D3 and D1 on simple polygonal GCs from #1229 (3.14.0, backported to 3.12.3 and 3.13.1). Regression scope: accurate for 1a, 1b, 1e and D3 (since 3.12.3/3.13.1/3.14.0) and for everything relative to 3.11.4; GC overlay on main is not worse overall than on 3.13.0, which threw 1356 TopologyExceptions in the 7872-result scan where main throws none. Two further mechanisms are documented in ISSUE.md but not claimed as contract violations: D4 (the GC's lines are pre-noded on their own in floating point, so rounded nodes lose exact coincidences: POINT(3 2) and GC(MULTILINESTRING((0 2,2 4),(0 4,6 0)), POINT(9 9)) intersect to POINT EMPTY), and D5 (a nested GEOMETRYCOLLECTION EMPTY makes a lineal GC 'mixed-dimension': clear IllegalArgumentException). The lead's cases in tests/crosscheck/test_overlay_crosscheck.py (GEOS_GC_OVERLAY, GEOS_GC_EMPTY_ASSERTION) are D1, D2 and D3. Upstream search: no duplicate on GitHub (libgeos/geos issues and PRs, shapely, jts); duckdb/duckdb-spatial#803 is a downstream report of D3. PostGIS trac was not searched (the egress proxy blocks trac.osgeo.org). libgeos/geos#948 is still open although its input has given the correct result since 3.13.1 (#1229); FINAL.md suggests it may be possible to close it. Different problems, checked: #696/#716 (OverlayNG simple-GC support, 3.12.0), #1023/#1050 (3.9 branch), #1059 (representation of an intersection with a GC of adjacent squares), #1316 (no GC); jts#667 and jts#833 are open JTS proposals for GC support (context only). families: the superseded lead's cases are corpus family 'empty'; the other cases come from the adversarial generator of tools/crosscheck_overlay.py. Nothing has been posted.

provenance.signature: relate and predicates (RelateNG) with valid GeometryCollection operands (documented as supported under union semantics), three independent defects: (D1, mixed GCs) TopologyComputer::addPointOnGeometry records Exterior x Interior = 2 and Exterior x Boundary = 1 for a Point element against an areal target even when the point lies in the target's exterior, and addLineEndOnGeometry records nothing for a line end on a Point element of a mixed target: GC(square [0,4]^2, POINT (10 10)) vs square [1,2]^2 gives 212FF1212 (exact 212FF1FF2, contains false); LINESTRING (0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0) is within GC(POINT (0 0), LINESTRING (5 5, 6 6)) (0FFFFF102, exact 0F1FFF102); (D2, overlapping GC polygons) RelateNode::addEdges checks the sector of a new area edge only after both edges of the section are inserted, so overlapping sections keep EXTERIOR sides and a point interior to the union is located on its boundary: GC(arrowhead, rectangle) vs POINT (2 1) gives FF20F1FF2 (exact 0F2FF1FF2: contains false, touches true); (D3, overlapping or adjacent GC polygons) away from the other operand the union boundary is seen only through each ring's first vertex (RelateNG::computeAreaVertex) and nodes where the GC's own polygons cross are never evaluated: four overlapping strips forming a 3x3 frame with a 1x1 hole equal the full square (2FFF1FFF2, exact 2FF11F2F2), and rings starting at a vertex interior to the union lose BE (FF2FFF102, exact FF2FF1102)

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, three GEOS reports and one JTS report: FINAL.md (D1), FINAL_2_overlapping_sections.md (D2) and FINAL_3_union_boundary.md (D3) for libgeos/geos, JTS_FINAL.md (sections 1 to 3) for locationtech/jts; the D2 and D3 patches must land together (ISSUE.md section 6). D3's first-vertex sub-case (d3-no-boundary-vertex) is the TODO at RelateNG.cpp:621 / RelateNG.java:507 ('use extremal (highest) point to ensure one is on boundary of polygon cluster') made concrete, not an unanticipated defect; that TODO's extremal-point idea would not fix the union-hole (frame) case, whose boundary contains no ring vertex. GEOS contradicts itself: relate(unaryUnion(A), B) is exact for D2 and D3 (not for D1, where the union is still a mixed GC; D1's evidence is contains without the far point and GEOS's own difference), and its point locator puts the frame's centre outside the frame. In the D1 line form GEOS's crosses = true is also the exact answer; only within and coveredBy are wrong there. In JTS, RelateNG is opt-in (GeometryRelate.RELATE_NG_DEFAULT = false), so JTS users meet these only through the RelateNG API or -Djts.relate=ng. No duplicate found: #1148 (fixed for 3.13.0 by the port of jts#1069) is the covered-element case, correct on main; #981, #982, #1022, #1027 and #1033 (the GC issues listed in #1060) give the expected answers on main; #983, #1011, #1147, #1149, #1275, jts#1052/#1055/#1073/#1089/#1090/#1099, jts#1175/#1200 (NTS #862) and the overlay issues #948, jts#784/#833 are different problems. The lead's other classes are covered by geos-relateng-line-end-skip (the GH-1201 covered-ring regression) and geos-relateng-segfault (the empty-element dimension case). The GEOS 3.13.0, 3.13.1 and 3.14.1 outputs were re-run when the review's corrections were applied (identical); the JTS test counts, the 29,719-case sweep and the 2.5x prototype cost are the triage's figures (output/). finding.toml proposes one entry per defect.

GEOS #1147/#1148/#1149, #1275, #983, #1022, #1027, #1064 and #1346 were checked and are different problems. The same triage found a second, separate cluster in covered-ring/: a GEOS 3.13.1 regression from GH-1201 (a port of locationtech/jts#1099) after which a linear or GeometryCollection operand B is no longer self-noded when A is polygonal, which makes contains, touches, covers and within wrong for valid polygon/line and polygon/GC pairs (covered-ring/FINAL.md, covered-ring/JTS_FINAL.md). provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage and by an independent review; not yet reported. One directory, two reports for locationtech/jts: FINAL.md (D1) and mixed-points/FINAL.md (D2, whose cases, repro and prototype fix are in mixed-points/); ISSUE.md is the full triage. No priority key because the entry covers both defects. D1 alone is low priority: it needs |ordinates| above about 1.3e162 (for these inputs) or a KdTree tolerance above 1.34e154, JTS documents no coordinate range, and the open, unmerged PR #1197 describes DD orientation as sound only for |coordinates| in about [2^-511, 2^511], so upstream may call such inputs out of range; it is still a silent wrong answer, a regression from 1.20.0 in unreleased code, with a one-line fix. D2 is normal priority: valid input with small, ordinary coordinates (0 to 7), through the documented fixed-PrecisionModel API. Both corpus cases need extreme coordinates (line-polygon-1-000090 at 3.8e220 for D1; point-geometry-1-000016 at about 1e-161 for D2, where the known orientation underflow of geos-tiny-coordinates-underflow collapses the small triangle), but neither defect is that mechanism. The tolerance-0 KdTree merge at the tiny end is older than #1114 (on master since #1112, whose MathUtil.hypot is a deliberate speed trade-off; also in 1.19.0 and earlier; only 1.20.0, with #923's Math.hypot, avoids it), so FINAL.md gives it as context and not as part of the regression. Related, none a duplicate: #1114, #1112/#1110, #923, #1187, #951, #1197, #295, #1133, geos#931, NTS#814 and PR NTS#848 (they port nearestNeighbor only, so NTS is unaffected for now), and GEOS 095c7270 (strict noding in 3.15+, not a fix for D2). NTS has the same (Polygon) cast as D2 (not run).

provenance.signature: booleanTouches, Polygon/MultiPolygon operands: decided from A's vertices only, and only from the first part of a MultiPolygon. Polygon/Polygon (index.ts L560-L581): touches = some vertex of A's outer ring on B's outer ring and no vertex of A strictly inside B; B's vertices, vertex-free interior overlap and holes as contact locations are never examined. So identical or overlapping polygons touch (POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0)) with itself: true, exact 2FFF1FFF2), and real touches are missed or depend on argument order (square [0,2]^2 and a triangle whose apex (1, 2) is on its top edge: touches(A, B) = false, touches(B, A) = true, exact FF2F01212). Polygon/MultiPolygon (L598) and MultiPolygon/MultiPolygon (L753) pass a single ring as a Polygon's coordinates, so the strictly-inside test never fires and A touches B as soon as a tested vertex of A lies on a ring of B's first part, even with A inside B (POLYGON ((2 0, 3 2, 1 2, 2 0)) and MULTIPOLYGON (((0 0, 4 0, 4 4, 0 4, 0 0))): true, exact 2FF10F212). MultiPolygon/MultiPolygon also bounds its vertex loop by the ring count (L731)

provenance.notes: Confirmed at triage; not yet reported (FINAL.md is the drafted report for Turfjs/turf). It contradicts booleanTouches' own doc ('true if none of the points common to both geometries intersect the interiors of both geometries') and the JSTS/Shapely touches that the package's test.ts compares against. No tolerance is involved: booleanPointOnLine is called without epsilon, and the 5 minimal cases use small integers (all float arithmetic exact). The four Polygon/Polygon fixtures (two true, two false) all pass the small square as feature1, and test.ts runs one argument order. Core tier: 404 of 2000 areal pairs wrong, and 70 of 207 integer-coordinate pairs (60 false positives). No duplicate: #3088 (open PR) fixes only the LineString/MultiLineString branch. Related, not duplicates: #1467 (open) raises the same vertex-only concern for booleanContains, which #3104 (7.4.0, closing #2242) addressed with edge splitting in isPolyInPoly (#1467's own example is exactly contains = true, and Turf 7.4.0 returns true); #3109 (open, v8) plans to replace isPolyInPoly. The lead's other parts are not new bugs. booleanOverlap is true on any edge contact: known, #2454 (open). ISSUE.md drafts an optional comment for #2454's unreported sub-case, containment with a shared boundary ([0,2]^2 and [0,1]^2: booleanOverlap = true and booleanContains = true, exact 212F11FF2). booleanContains ignores holes: known, #1882, and #3109 plans the rewrite. booleanOverlap's geojsonEquality precision 6 and booleanContains' BOUNDARY_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE 1e-6 are by-design tolerances (RFC 7946 rationale in the source). A few near-miss touches/overlaps flips are float robustness, and Turf claims no exactness. Out of scope, noted in ISSUE.md: the MultiLineString/MultiPoint branch indexes lines with the MultiPoint index (L336, L344). An independent review's corrections were applied (7.0.0 re-run with pinned dependencies, L598/L753 root cause, hole wording, fixture count; see ISSUE.md). Nothing has been posted.

Related, not duplicates: #1467 (open) raises the same vertex-only concern for booleanContains, which #3104 (7.4.0, closing #2242) addressed with edge splitting in isPolyInPoly (#1467's own example is exactly contains = true, and Turf 7.4.0 returns true); #3109 (open, v8) plans to replace isPolyInPoly. The lead's other parts are not new bugs. booleanOverlap is true on any edge contact: known, #2454 (open). ISSUE.md drafts an optional comment for #2454's unreported sub-case, containment with a shared boundary ([0,2]^2 and [0,1]^2: booleanOverlap = true and booleanContains = true, exact 212F11FF2). booleanContains ignores holes: known, #1882, and #3109 plans the rewrite. booleanOverlap's geojsonEquality precision 6 and booleanContains' BOUNDARY_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE 1e-6 are by-design tolerances (RFC 7946 rationale in the source). A few near-miss touches/overlaps flips are float robustness, and Turf claims no exactness. Out of scope, noted in ISSUE.md: the MultiLineString/MultiPoint branch indexes lines with the MultiPoint index (L336, L344). An independent review's corrections were applied (7.0.0 re-run with pinned dependencies, L598/L753 root cause, hole wording, fixture count; see ISSUE.md). Nothing has been posted.
